story.iWant: to create a configuration system for API keys and settings
story.soThat: I can manage environment variables securely and access them throughout the application
story.tasks: - Create configuration module structure (AC: #1) - Create `/src/bet_bot/config/` directory (if not exists) - Create `/src/bet_bot/config/__init__.py` - Create `/src/bet_bot/config/settings.py` as main config file - Import Pydantic BaseModel and Field - Define Pydantic Config model (AC: #1, #3, #4) - Create `Config` class inheriting from `pydantic.BaseModel` - Add required field: `openai_api_key` (mapped from `OPENAI_API_KEY` env var) - Add required field: `api_football_key` (mapped from `API_FOOTBALL_KEY` env var) - Add optional field: `odds_api_key` with default `None` (mapped from `ODDS_API_KEY` env var) - Add optional field: `log_level` with default `"INFO"` (mapped from `LOG_LEVEL` env var) - Use Pydantic `Field()` with descriptions for each field - Set `ConfigDict` to allow population by field name - Test: Can instantiate Config with valid data - Implement environment variable loading (AC: #2) - Import `dotenv.load_dotenv` - Import `os` for environment variable access - Call `load_dotenv()` at module load time - Read all config values from `os.getenv()` - Pass to `Config()` constructor - Test: `.env` file loaded correctly - Add validation logic (AC: #5, #6) - Create validators for `openai_api_key` and `api_football_key` - Validate keys are not empty strings (length > 0) - Validate keys don't contain obvious placeholder values - Add model-level `validate()` classmethod for startup validation - Raise `ValueError` with clear message if validation fails - Test: Missing required keys raises helpful error - Create singleton config instance (AC: #7) - Create module-level `config` instance: `config = Config()` - Export from `__init__.py` so importable as `from bet_bot.config import config` - Add docstring explaining singleton pattern - Test: Can import and access config from anywhere - Create startup validation hook (AC: #5, #6) - Create `validate_config()` function - Check all required keys are present and non-empty - Log validation results - Return boolean (True if valid, False otherwise) - Provide clear error messages for each missing key - Export function for use in CLI main - Add masked logging support (AC: #5) - Create `get_masked_key(key)` method in Config class - Return masked version: `key[:4]...key[-4:]` (or "****" if too short) - Use for safe debugging without exposing full keys - Document this pattern in docstring - Update `.env.template` (AC: all) - Create `.env.template` in project root if missing - Include placeholders for: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `API_FOOTBALL_KEY`, `ODDS_API_KEY`, `LOG_LEVEL` - Add comments explaining each variable - Commit to git (template, not actual secrets) - Integration with CLI (AC: all) - Import Config in `/src/bet_bot/cli/main.py` - Call `config.validate()` at startup - Show clear error and exit if validation fails - Test: CLI fails gracefully if config invalid - Documentation and validation (AC: all) - Add docstrings to Config class explaining each field - Add comments explaining validation logic - Document .env file format - Test: All configuration flows work as expected

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Create `Pydantic` config model (`Config` class in `/src/bet_bot/config/`) 2. Load from `.env` file using `python-dotenv` 3. Define required fields: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `API_FOOTBALL_KEY` 4. Define optional fields: `ODDS_API_KEY`, `LOG_LEVEL` 5. Validate API keys are not empty on startup 6. Raise clear error if required keys missing 7. Store config singleton accessible from anywhere

doc.title: bet-bot Project Rules - API Key Management
doc.snippet: CRITICAL (ZERO TOLERANCE): ALWAYS store API keys in environment variables (NEVER in code). ALWAYS validate API keys exist at startup. ALWAYS use python-dotenv for local development. NEVER log API keys (even partially - use masking). ALWAYS use different keys for dev/staging/prod.

doc.title: bet-bot Project Rules - Configuration Pattern
doc.snippet: Load environment variables with load_dotenv(). Create Config class inheriting from pydantic.BaseModel. Define required fields with aliases for env vars. Implement Config.validate() classmethod for startup checks. Raise ValueError with clear message if validation fails. Create singleton instance: config = Config().

python.package: Schema validation and configuration models - core dependency for Config class
Environment variable loading from .env files - required for load_dotenv() function
CLI framework - already installed, used for error handling and exit codes in config validation
Type hints support - required for Optional, ConfigDict types in Config class

constraints.constraint: MANDATORY: Store ALL API keys in environment variables - NEVER hardcode in source code (CLAUDE.md requirement)
MANDATORY: Validate API keys exist and are non-empty on application startup (CLAUDE.md requirement)
MANDATORY: Use python-dotenv for loading environment variables from .env file (CLAUDE.md requirement)
MANDATORY: NEVER log full API keys - use get_masked_key() method for any debugging output (CLAUDE.md requirement)
MANDATORY: .env file MUST be in .gitignore - prevent accidental secret commits (CLAUDE.md requirement)
Use Pydantic BaseModel for config validation - allows field validation, type checking, and population by field name
Required fields: openai_api_key, api_football_key - must raise clear error if missing at startup
Optional fields: odds_api_key (default None), log_level (default "INFO") - should not block startup if missing
Use Field() with descriptions for each config field - improves code documentation and IDE hints
Implement ConfigDict to allow population by field name - enables flexible env var naming and testing
Create module-level singleton instance `config = Config()` - accessible from anywhere as `from bet_bot.config import config`
Implement validate_config() function for explicit startup validation - called from CLI main before any command execution
Config class must have get_masked_key(key: str) method - returns masked version like "sk-proj-****[...]**** " for safe logging
Create .env.template in project root - document all required and optional variables with comments, commit to git (not secrets)
Integrate with CLI (Story 1.3) - call config.validate() in main.py callback, show clear error and exit(1) if validation fails
All docstrings must explain validation behavior and secure key handling - developers should understand the security model

interface.name: Config Class
interface.signature: class Config(BaseModel): openai_api_key: str, api_football_key: str, odds_api_key: Optional[str] = None, log_level: str = "INFO"

tests.standards: Testing framework: pytest 8.4.2 with pytest-asyncio for async support and monkeypatch for environment variable mocking. All config tests should be in tests/unit/test_config.py. Use monkeypatch fixture to mock environment variables and os.getenv() calls. Test both validation success and failure paths. Mock load_dotenv() to isolate unit tests from actual .env files. Minimum 80% code coverage required for config module. Test data validation, type conversion, error handling, and secure key masking.
